scope: Proposition 3.10 (Reduction of the numerical theorem) of the manuscript “A Charged Reduction of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality in Spatial Dimensions at Least Four” (preprints/A-Charged-Reduction-of-the-Spacetime-Penrose-Inequality-in-Spatial-Dimensions-at-Least-Four-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3e5e445d305051a1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume that for every prepared data set in (3.15), with positive energy and zero momentum, the construction of Proposition 6.6 establishes, for every 0 < s < 1, EADM ≥ s|Q| + 1 − s2 2 ( a ω )(k−1)/k . (3.20) Then Theorem 2.5 follows for the original purely electric data. The same inequality with invariant mass in place of energy holds on the strict, future-timelike auxiliary magnetic class described above.
